title: mut.channel_halloran_cyanotype_celestial
mutation_directive: Lia Halloran — Your Body Is A Space That Sees — Your Body Is A Space That Sees (LAX Terminal 2/3 installation, 2022; Harvard Plate Stacks acquisition). VISUAL SIGNATURE: Deep Prussian-blue field with white-negative-space stars, comets, and figures — cyanotype contact prints of brushstroked transparencies. Star fields and orbital diagrams overlaid with painterly drips, giving cosmos a hand-painted-photographic warmth. The blue is unmistakable: ferric ammonium citrate's cyan. TECHNICAL HOOKS for three.js / GLSL: Particles scattered as a galactic-coordinate distribution (concentrated along a Milky-Way band, sparse in halos). Render against a Prussian-blue (#0d2c54) background; particles are small white-glow sprites with Gaussian falloff. Add a second layer: a flowing 'brushstroke' SDF (computed in fragshader) that erodes/grows based on simplex noise — wherever the brushstroke is, particles brighten. Result: hand-painted constellation maps. Palette is locked to cyanotype blue + paper-white. WHY DIVERSE: Pool has zero blue/photographic register. All current pieces are dark-mode-with-bright-particles or grayscale. This adds a totally different palette anchored in 19th-century photochemistry, plus a feminist astronomy narrative. Stay faithful to the visual signature; pick whatever three.js primitives are needed (Lines2 / InstancedMesh / SphereGeometry / custom ShaderMaterial) — but the FORM should read as if this artist made it. REF: https://liahalloran.com/your-body-is-a-space-that-sees
